title: Military Discourse as A Linguistic Phenomenon: Lexical, Semantic, and Pragmatic Dimensions of Modern Military English
authors: Rymma Maiboroda
venue: International Journal of Social Science Humanity & Management Research
abstract: The present article investigates Military English as a specific type of institutional discourse characterized by lexical specialization, semantic mitigation, and pragmatic control. Drawing on critical discourse analysis, cognitive linguistics, and register theory, the study examines how military language functions simultaneously as a technical communication system and as an ideological instrument, shaping both operational and social realities. Particular attention is paid to the use of specialized terminology, acronyms, euphemisms, metaphorical expressions, and grammatical structures that regulate internal military communication, command execution, and public representations of armed conflict. The analysis highlights how military discourse frames actions, structures perceptions, obscures agency, and legitimizes institutional decisions while managing emotional and social responses to warfare. The study also explores neologisms and lexical borrowings that have emerged in response to contemporary military events, demonstrating the adaptive and dynamic nature of Military English in the Ukrainian context. By integrating authentic military texts, media reports, and instructional materials, the research provides a comprehensive account of the linguistic mechanisms through which authority, responsibility, and operational efficiency are enacted and communicated. The article contributes to philological and sociolinguistic research by offering insights into how language functions not merely as a medium of description but as a constitutive instrument of military practice, shaping ideology, perception, and collective understanding of conflict and defenсe.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Ensemble Framework for Haze Degree Estimation in Vision-Based Processing Systems
authors: Garima Kadian; Rajiv Kumar
abstract: Abstract Haze severely degrades outdoor image visibility and color fidelity, limiting the reliability of vision-based systems used in autonomous navigation, environmental monitoring, and aerial surveillance. Existing haze degree estimation approaches either rely on handcrafted priors with limited generalization or deep learning models that behave as black boxes without awareness of uncertainty. To address this gap, we present a Hybrid Haze Degree Estimation (HHDE) framework that integrates interpretable physical haze descriptors with high-level convolutional representations within a probabilistic ensemble learning paradigm. Nineteen haze-relevant features are fused with CNN embeddings and processed using a stacking architecture consisting of Random Forest and XGBoost regressors. At the same time, a Bayesian Ridge meta-learner produces uncertainty-aware haze predictions. HHDE quantifies both haze degree and its corresponding confidence interval, improving reliability in uncertain atmospheric conditions. Extensive evaluation on ten benchmark datasets demonstrates the superior performance of HHDE over classical regression algorithms and state-of-the-art deep learning models, achieving an MAE of 0.0206, an RMSE of 0.0301, and an $R^2$ of 0.9525. Ablation analyses confirm the complementary roles of hybrid feature fusion and Bayesian reasoning. The results establish HHDE as a robust, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware solution suitable for real-world environmental image analysis and autonomous vision systems.

title: Cross-Cultural Narrative Translation and Communication Effects of Chinese Online Literature: A Case Study of Lord of the Mysteries
authors: YuWen Qian
abstract: This paper explores Chinese online literature’s shift from “going out” to “going in” with Lord of the Mysteries as a case. It analyzes cross-cultural narratives at worldview and value levels and examines reader sentiment via WebNovel comments. While feedback is largely positive and generates emotional resonance, cultural identification remains implicit. Overseas communication should balance cultural uniqueness and narrative intelligibility.

title: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models
authors: Aviv Yossef; Or Patashnik; Or Zamir
abstract: We present a provably distortion-free semantic watermarking algorithm that requires only black-box sampling access to a generative model and black-box access to a semantic embedding. A watermark is called distortion-free if, averaged over its secret detection key, it leaves the generator's output distribution unchanged; this provides a formal guarantee that watermarking does not reduce output quality. Conventional such watermarks are often brittle to transformations. This is especially problematic for images, where benign operations such as compression, cropping, or resizing change the entire pixel representation. Semantic watermarks therefore require detection to be robust to content-preserving transformations. Previous methods combining these properties rely heavily on specific white-box properties of the underlying model: either to autoregressive text generation or to diffusion-specific access, such as control of the initial noise or diffusion inversion. In contrast, our construction is fully generic: It only interacts with the generative model and the semantic embedding, a function that determines the notion of "preserving content" under which detection should be robust, via sample and query access. We then instantiate this framework for image generation. We characterize the two competing properties required of the semantic embedding: it should remain stable under transformations that preserve an image's content, but should distinguish independent generations from the same prompt. We train an image encoder directly for this tradeoff. The resulting encoder improves separation while maintaining stability over off-the-shelf alternatives and enables strong aggregate detection while remaining robust to various transformations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our watermark scheme on both open-source and closed models, which is possible only due to restriction to black-box access.

title: TextSphere: Efficient Text-to-Image Generation via Shared Hyperspherical Alignment and Uniformity
authors: Yixia Zhang; Girish A. Koushik; Xilu Wang; Wenwu Wang
abstract: Recent advances in text-to-image generation have substantially improved image quality, particularly through diffusion-based methods that require multiple inference steps. In contrast, Sphere Encoder offers an efficient generative framework capable of producing images with fewer forward steps. However, extending it to free-form text is nontrivial, because its class-conditioned design lacks cross-modal alignment. To address this challenge, we propose TextSphere, an efficient text-to-image generative framework that extends Sphere Encoder with language conditioning and cross-modal alignment. We incorporate pretrained CLIP text embeddings through adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN) to guide image generation while retaining the original spherical sampling mechanism. To bridge the cross-modal representation gap, we introduce a Spherical Semantic Alignment and Uniformity (SSAU) objective that jointly promotes semantic alignment and representation uniformity on the hypersphere. Experiments on CUB-200-2011, MS-COCO-2014, and Flickr30k demonstrate that TextSphere consistently reduces generation FID (gFID) over the text-conditioned baseline while achieving reconstruction FID (rFID) below 1.0. With only 4 and 6 sampling steps, TextSphere achieves lower gFID than the compared diffusion- and GAN-based models trained from scratch on CUB-200-2011 and MS-COCO-2014, respectively. We further observe that improved reconstruction fidelity does not necessarily yield better generation quality. In addition, we use Partial Least Squares Singular Value Decomposition (PLS-SVD) to analyze cross-modal alignment and modality gap, offering insight into the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation
authors: Xiaoyu Wu; Yifei Wang; Weihang Guo; Chen Wei; Lydia E Kavraki; Niloofar Mireshghallah; Steven Wu
abstract: Pixel-space diffusion learns visual representations and image generation jointly in a single end-to-end training stage, without a separately pretrained visual encoder. However, plain pixel-space Transformers still trail leading two-stage latent diffusion models in generation quality and training efficiency. We hypothesize that part of this gap arises from retaining one token per patch throughout the backbone, which does not explicitly encourage a visual hierarchy that summarizes related content at progressively coarser levels. To address this, we introduce Hierarchical Diffusion Transformers (HiT), which progressively group related tokens and represent each group with a single token. The main Transformer bottleneck processes these compact group tokens, and ungrouping restores features to their original image positions. A compression budget regulates the average compression ratio across the batch, allowing group memberships and counts to vary across images and diffusion timesteps during both training and generation. The model exhibits emergent semantic structure, learning to group coherent objects and object parts without segmentation labels. In text-to-image generation, HiT further learns to group caption words with image patches depicting the same concepts, without region annotations. HiT achieves 1.48 FID on ImageNet $256\times256$ and reaches comparable generation quality to JiT using approximately 40\% of its cumulative training FLOPs. For text-to-image generation, HiT exceeds UniLiP's average score across five benchmarks with roughly $6\times$ fewer denoiser parameters and $3\times$ fewer forward FLOPs. These results suggest that learning a visual hierarchy within the generator breaks down the barrier to stronger image generation without external visual pretraining.

title: Beyond Attribute-Centric Fairness: Modelling and Mitigating Unified Bias Representation in Omni-modal Large Language Models
authors: Runqi Lin; Suqin Yuan; Zihao Fu; Chris Russell
abstract: Omni-modal large language models (OLLMs) provide joint multimodal understanding and generation capabilities, making them well-suited to complex environments and promising backbones for next-generation AI. Despite these advances, the harmful stereotypes encoded in such models manifest in increasingly diverse forms, leading to broader and more severe societal consequences. Existing debiasing methods typically impose separate fairness objectives for each sensitive attribute and modality to minimise demographic-dependent variations. However, in omni-modal settings, this attribute-centric paradigm struggles to jointly address diverse social biases with distinct fairness objectives and to generalise beyond predefined attributes. To this end, we propose OmniDebias, one of the first methods for promoting fairness in OLLMs, which employs a bias-centric formulation to extract and mitigate a shared bias representation across attributes and modalities while preserving attribute-related knowledge. Specifically, we exploit activation inconsistencies of a given attribute (e.g., gender) across semantic contexts (e.g., occupations) to disentangle bias from legitimate knowledge. We further consolidate multiple extracted biases into a shared representation, formulating a unified objective that captures the underlying structure across social biases and generalises to unseen attributes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that eliminating unified bias with both post-hoc editing and fine-tuning can consistently improve fairness across diverse attributes and modalities in OLLMs while maintaining favourable utility.

title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
authors: Guoqing Wang; Pin Tang; Xiangxuan Ren; Chao Ma
abstract: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations. However, most world VLA models generate future frames at the pixel level with plenty of dense visual tokens. Although such generated futures can be visually plausible, they preserve many driving-irrelevant appearance details, i.e., only a small portion of the tokens directly encode critical planning-relevant factors, such as agent geometry, motion dynamics, and interactions. This introduces a significant performance bottleneck. An important question thus arises: what world state should a world VLA model reason over to support planning beyond pixel-level prediction? We argue that planning-oriented world modeling should focus on a compact and structured agent-centric latent state that captures the interactions between objects in the driving scene over time. As such, we introduce AgentWorld, an agent-centric VLA world model that uses discrete agent tokens jointly for reasoning and trajectory planning. Each token is dynamically grounded to a surrounding agent associated with its object's state, such as semantic identity, 3D geometry, motion, and interaction context. AgentWorld learns these tokens through three key processes: explicit geometric grounding, reasoning-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and agent-oriented reinforcement learning. Extensive open-loop and closed-loop experiments under diverse driving scenarios show that AgentWorld enhances planning capabilities, fully exploits visual evidence and agent dynamics, and yields interpretable agent-centric world states.

title: CascadeJEPA: Enhancing 3D Geometric Representations via Spatially Coupled Cascaded Prediction
authors: Kailai Zhou; Ziqi Chen; Xiaoning Xu; Yuefeng Wu; Zixuan Fu; Zijun Lin; Zhihao Li; Youwei Pang; Xiaoqi Zhao; Xun Cao; Bihan Wen
abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for predictive visual representation learning. However, our analysis of I-JEPA reveals a growing discrepancy between semantic and geometric learning: improved semantic recognition during pretraining is accompanied by degraded 3D geometric representations. We hypothesize that this partly stems from predicting highly abstract latent representations with incomplete spatial context, favoring semantic regularities over fine-grained geometric information. To address this issue, we introduce CascadeJEPA, a spatially coupled cascaded prediction framework that promotes richer patch-level interactions through full-grid context encoding and cross-attention between prediction stages, while largely preserving the original I-JEPA architecture. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements over I-JEPA across multiple 3D geometric tasks while maintaining strong semantic recognition performance. Furthermore, its advantages extend to future feature forecasting and world model planning, highlighting the potential of enhanced geometric representations to support predictive world modeling.

title: Semantic-Guided Geometric Decoding for Token-Efficient Visual Grounding
authors: Zhaojie Chen; Junyan Yang; Le Yang; Qi Dang; Yucheng Huang; Qianyi Che; Zhaoqiang Chen; Xinqi Zhu; Qiang Zhao
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) provide a unified interface for language-conditioned visual perception. In pixel-to-sequence grounding, autoregressive coordinate generation requires multiple sequential decoding steps per box, increasing inference cost with the number of instances. Pixel-to-embedding methods reduce this overhead but lack explicit spatial encoding when using a shared special token. We introduce SemGeo, a token-efficient visual grounding framework that represents each instance with a single grid token for coarse localization. A geometric decoder reuses visual features and hidden states to recover precise discrete box coordinates in parallel. To train proposal generation and box localization together, we introduce Gaussian soft labels that encode coordinate distances during supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Reinforcement post-training further combines box-set rewards with coordinate supervision on model-generated proposals. This stage trains the language model and geometric decoder on their own predictions to mitigate the mismatch between teacher-forced training and inference. Across eight benchmarks spanning object detection, referring object detection, and document layout grounding, SemGeo achieves the highest F1@mIou among compared MLLMs on six benchmarks. It also delivers $2.07\times$ and $1.25\times$ the mean box-generation throughput of representative grounding baselines under vLLM and Transformers, respectively, while achieving higher accuracy in both comparisons.

title: BehaVerify: A Formal Verification Tool for Behavior Trees
authors: Serena S. Serbinowska; Ben Wooding; Diego Manzanas Lopez; Luke Nam; Anne M. Tumlin; Nicholas K. Potteiger; Hongchao Zhang; Taylor T. Johnson
abstract: This paper presents BehaVerify, a verification toolbox for behavior trees (BTs) and Neuro-Symbolic BTs. BTs are a graphical language for planning and sequencing behaviors - similar to extended state machines - and are increasingly used in safety-critical domains. BehaVerify enables users to specify a BT using a Domain Specific Language (DSL) with formal syntax and semantics. This language further includes Linear Temporal Logic and Computation Tree Logic specifications. BehaVerify uses an efficient encoding into nuXmv, called fastforwarding, to quickly verify if a specification holds over the BT. Additionally, BehaVerify can generate implementations of the BT in Python and Haskell. Through Python, BehaVerify has been integrated with PyTrees and Robot Operating System (ROS) and has been deployed to several autonomous robotic systems, including for verifying runtime monitors. While prior works have developed the underlying theory, this manuscript focuses on the toolbox usage, functionality and implementation. BehaVerify is open source: https://github.com/verivital/behaverify

title: From Constraints to Causality: Petri net Encodings for Explaining Binary Neural Network Inference
authors: Alex Chan; Mohamed Tarraf; Alex Yakovlev; Rishad Shafik
abstract: Binary Neural Networks (BNNs) are attractive for resource-constrained hardware and on-device components in autonomous systems. However, their discrete, non-linear behaviour makes them difficult to analyse and trust in safety-relevant settings. Existing approaches based on SAT and Satisfiability Modulo Theories can verify a BNN's input-output properties, but treat it as a monolithic constraint system, which reveal only whether a property holds and not how the computation reaches its result. In this paper, we present an early work that provides a complementary, discrete-event view. We give a compositional translation from the inference semantics of a fixed, trained BNN to a 1-safe Petri net (PN), where each computation step is an explicit transition, so that a firing sequence is a causal trace of the BNN's decision. On a worked example, we establish faithfulness via exhaustive input-output equivalence against a reference implementation, and show how contrasting firing sequences localises where a single-feature change alters the prediction. Finally, we outline two directions this opens: a correctness-of-translation theorem, and a causal-trace analysis of where two trained BNNs diverge in their decisions, a structural question that constraint-based verifiers cannot express.

title: DAP-MR: Degradation-Aware Prompt-Magnitude Routing for Real-World Ultrasound Super-Resolution
authors: Ngoc-Hoang-Lam Le; Thi-An Le; Dinh-Hung Le; Manh-Hung Nguyen; Kai-Lung Hua; Ching-Chun Huang
abstract: When super-resolution models designed for natural images are used on ultrasound scans, relying on semantic text prompts can lead to unreliable results. The tags these models generate often do not match the actual restoration needs, and specialized medical terms may be misunderstood by general-purpose text encoders. Instead, prompts focused on common image degradations are more directly useful for guiding restoration. However, using a single prompt to describe both the type and severity of image degradation can entangle these factors, making it hard for the model to know how strong the degradation is. To address this limitation, we introduce Degradation-Aware Prompt--Magnitude Routing (DAP-MR). Each degradation type is represented by a dedicated token initialized from the contextualized EOS embedding of a degradation-oriented prompt and subsequently adapted during ultrasound SR training. A separate magnitude router predicts a continuous, input-dependent magnitude that modulates the corresponding token. Thus, language provides a degradation-aware initialization for what should be restored, while magnitude routing supplies an explicit signal for how strongly it should influence restoration. DAP-MR can be added to both one-step and multi-step diffusion super-resolution frameworks without changing their core structures. Our experiments--on synthetic datasets with both in-domain and under anatomical-domain shift, as well as unpaired real-world ultrasound data--show that DAP-MR delivers better restoration quality and generalizes more consistently across different domains.

title: AnalogMorph: evaluating representation fidelity in LLM analog netlist reasoning
authors: Wei Zhen Leong; Steve Gunn; Jing Huey Khor
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly adopted to augment analog integrated circuit design, yet existing studies primarily evaluate circuit recognition accuracy on canonical representations while largely overlooking representation fidelity. In analog design, electrically identical circuits may be represented using arbitrary device indices, net names, transistor ordering, and structural decompositions. Human designers recognize these representations as equivalent, yet LLM behavior under such transformations is not well characterized. This work introduces AnalogMorph, a metamorphic benchmark applying three topology-preserving transformations (device-net permutation, both constructive and deceptive semantic keyword injection) to curated topologies. The benchmark evaluates whether circuit interpretations remain consistent when electrical connectivity is unchanged. The suitability of a structure-aware encoding based on the device–net incidence matrix with breadth-first electrical position ordering is further examined. Within the evaluated settings, experimental results reveal substantial sensitivity of contemporary LLMs to electrically irrelevant textual cues. Although structure-aware representations can alter model behavior, their benefits are highly model-dependent, indicating that representation engineering alone does not guarantee robust circuit understanding. These findings position AnalogMorph as a diagnostic complement to recognition accuracy for evaluating representation-robust and trustworthy analog design assistants.

title: TICK: Text-Informed Contrastive Kernels for Probabilistic Time-Series Retrieval
authors: Rayen Ben Masseoud; Faïcel Chamroukhi
abstract: The coexistence of sensor data and textual knowledge across industrialapplications highlights the need to align natural language withmultivariate time series. This challenge is typically treated as adeterministic task, ignoring the fact that a vague query may matchhundreds of recordings while a precise one matches only a few. We arguethat text-to-time-series retrieval is inherently a probabilisticcross-modal problem and propose TICK, a framework in which each textquery carries a learned uncertainty $\sigma_t$ reflecting how many timeseries are semantically compatible with it. Without supervising $\sigma_t$directly, we find that it tracks query specificity with Spearmancorrelations $\rho \in [-0.88, -0.75]$ on three independent industrialbenchmarks. We further show that coupling the time-series representationto the text query is a necessary condition for this calibration to emerge:without it, $\sigma_t$ collapses to a constant, eliminating the model'sability to adapt its retrieval scope to query specificity. Because$\sigma_t$ sets the retrieval scope of a query, TICK spends a query-dependentcandidate budget instead of a fixed worst-case one, on top of a frozen33M-parameter sentence encoder and a small patch Transformer, with no languagemodel in the inference loop.

title: Scaling Channel-Adaptive Self-Supervised Learning
authors: Alice V. De Lorenci; Seungeun Yi; Theo Moutakanni; Piotr Bojanowski; Camille Couprie; Juan C. Caicedo; Wolfgang M. Pernice
abstract: Recent advances in self-supervised pre-training of foundation models for natural images have made them a popular choice for various visual systems and applications. Self-supervised strategies are also promising in non-RGB scientific imaging domains such as in biology, medical and satellite imagery, but their broader application is hampered by heterogeneity in channel composition and semantics between relevant datasets: two datasets may contain different numbers of channels, and these may reveal distinct aspects of an object or scene. Recent works on channel adaptive strategies report substantial advantages for those that account for variable channel compositions without sacrificing the ability to jointly encode channels; yet, how these strategies behave at scale remains unclear. We here show that, surprisingly, trained across large-scale datasets, independent-encoding of channels outperforms joint-encoding methods by a substantial margin. We validate this result along an extensive set of experiments on various datasets from cell microscopy to geospatial imagery. Our DINO BoC approach sets a new state-of-the-art across challenging benchmarks, including generalization to out-of-distribution tasks and unseen channel combinations. We open-source code and model weights for a new general-purpose feature extractor for fluorescent microscopy.

title: QVS-LIVO RiskMap: Health- and Information-Aware View Selection for Multi-Camera LIVO and Off-Road Risk Mapping
authors: Zihan Pan; Jinghan Wang; Hang Li; Feng Cheng; Tianchen Liu; Gaoliang Peng
abstract: Multi-camera observations in off-road environments vary significantly in reliability, posing challenges when complementing degraded geometric constraints. Motivated by this, we propose Quality-aware View Selection Lidar-Vision Odometry Risk Mapping (QVS-LIVO RiskMap), which decouples visual processing for state estimation from that for semantic mapping. The front end evaluates camera observations through read-only pretracking on a shared lidar-inertial posterior, combining observation health with geometric complementarity. Channel health memory and switching hysteresis govern selection of at most one eligible view for direct photometric correction. The posterior is retained when no view is eligible or the correction fails acceptance. The mapping back end integrates semantic observations from all available views in a shared world grid. Vehicle-scale geometry constrains semantic risk corrections, while spatial and temporal evidence supports risk confirmation. The system also produces a local bird's-eye-view (BEV) risk map and a global 2.5D semantic-terrain risk map with obstacle instance voxels. On two field sequences, QVS-LIVO achieved horizontal root mean square errors of 0.910 m and 1.664 m. It reduced error by 43.3% relative to FAST-LIO2 on the degraded long-route sequence. Across 12 controlled camera-fault configurations involving dropout, black frames and 60 ms timestamp shifts, it maintained complete trajectories with errors of 1.54-2.23 m. When deployed onboard an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the system generates local and global maps at 9.94 Hz and 2.00 Hz, respectively, with a median local mapping latency of 32.4 ms. These runtime results demonstrate the real-time feasibility of selective visual state updates alongside multi-view semantic mapping under challenging off-road conditions. The code and related resources are available at: https://github.com/zihanPan-HIT/QVS-LIVO.

title: BiRefNet-V2: Rethinking Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation
authors: Peng Zheng; Deng-Ping Fan; Binglu Wang; Nicu Sebe
abstract: Dichotomous image segmentation requires pixel-accurate foreground-background separation while preserving fine structures such as thin filaments, sharp edges, and intricate textures. BiRefNet addressed this challenge through bilateral references, combining image patches and gradient information, but its inward reference loses local spatial structure and lacks semantic guidance, while its outward reference relies on single-channel gradient attention. We recast this paradigm as controlled information recovery - locality determines what spatial information survives, semantic selectivity what information enters, and focused boundary supervision where refinement occurs - and propose BiRefNet-V2 to implement it: (1) locality-preserving and semantically guided detail injection through space-to-depth transformation, overlapping patches, and a Semantically Guided Gate; (2) a learned boundary stream with focused supervision that generates full-channel residual attention without requiring boundary annotations; and (3) a dual-branch decoder integrating depth-wise boundary convolutions with large-kernel attention. A modernized framework - LayerNorm, GELU, the Lion optimizer, and a DINOv3 backbone - cuts training from 600 to 50 epochs. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on DIS5K, camouflaged object detection, and high-resolution salient object detection across all 13 evaluation sets. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet-V2.

title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
authors: Liu Hung Ming; Tian Xia
abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. A corrected explicit-silence cost makes 18/20 policies fully silent and lowers mean sending to .050, but its strict complete-suppression gate fails because two seeds retain communication. Failed semantic-evasion and operational gates further bound the result. The evidence supports adaptive reallocation of a joint message--route code under partial monitoring, not open-world route discovery, emergent encryption, or a universal defense.

title: Disentangling Channel Semantics in Vision Transformers via Token Decorrelation and Composition-Aware Modulation
authors: Daeun Kim; Hyesong Choi; Hyejin Park; Dongbo Min
abstract: Multi-channel images encode heterogeneous channel semantics aligned over a shared spatial structure, which requires models to jointly capture globally shared structure and channel-specific variations. Recent multi-channel Vision Transformers attempt to address this challenge by augmenting the [CLS] token with memory tokens to organize multi-channel representations under varying channel compositions. However, we find that these context tokens collapse onto a few dominant channels under high inter-channel redundancy, producing redundant representations and a biased global summary that fails to reliably support composition-aware channel interpretation. We propose MuCa-ViT (Multi-Channel Composition-Aware Vision Transformer), a unified framework that addresses these limitations through two coupled mechanisms. Factorial Token Learning (FTL) enforces token-level decorrelation among context tokens, encouraging the [CLS] token to capture globally shared semantics while memory tokens preserve complementary channel-specific cues. Channel Composition-Aware Modulation (CAM) uses the FTL-refined [CLS] as a semantic anchor to generate sample-wise modulation signals, which enable composition-aware interpretation of channels within a unified backbone rather than relying on static channel embeddings. Experiments on JUMP-CP, CHAMMI, and So2Sat show that MuCa-ViT outperforms prior multi-channel ViTs across all three benchmarks, and the magnitude of improvement aligns with the inter-channel redundancy of each dataset ($ρ\in [0.19, 0.77]$), validating the diagnostic analysis that motivates our design. Our code is available at https://github.com/kimdanni/MuCa-ViT .

title: Computational Studies of Triplet State Formation in Zinc Dipyrrin Complexes
authors: Reuben Kwabla Adigbli
venue: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University)
abstract: Zinc dipyrromethene complexes are promising earth-abundant photosensitizers due to their strong visible-light absorption and tunable excited states. To rationally design them for photocatalysis and photodynamic therapy, a molecular-level understanding of triplet-state formation is needed, but details of intersystem crossing remain unclear. To study the effect of π-extension, we synthesized an indole-substituted zinc dipyrrin complex: the dipyrromethane ligand was prepared from indole and mesitaldehyde, oxidized to the dipyrromethene, then coordinated with zinc. DFT and TD-DFT calculations determined ground and excited-state geometries and energies in different solvents, modeled absorption spectra, and visualized charge distributions. The results show how solvent polarity shifts energies of the ground, lowest triplet, and excited singlet states, and influences charge separation in the excited state. These computational findings, coupled with photophysical measurements, will establish a framework for designing zinc dipyrrin complexes with improved triplet state yield.

title: PRISM-Net: Patient-specific reference-guided inter-breast symmetry matching for three-class breast DCE-MRI classification
authors: Boya Zhang; Shuaiwen Zhou; Di Kong; Mingxu Wang; Wenbiao Du; Yiman Zhong; Yuexin Duan; Xiawei Yue; Liuquan Cheng; Xiru Li
abstract: Abstract Breast DCE-MRI classification of breast sides as no lesion, benign, or malignant is complicated by substantial patient-specific variation in breast anatomy, tissue composition, and physiological enhancement. Although radiologists routinely use the contralateral breast as an internal reference, computational bilateral comparison remains challenging because corresponding contralateral regions are not anatomically identical and bilateral differences are not necessarily pathological. We propose PRISM-Net, a registration-free bilateral framework that treats the contralateral breast as an approximate patient-specific reference. PRISM-Net learns complementary target-appearance and reference-conditioned deviation representations. Adaptive patch-level matching constructs content-dependent contralateral references in a shared feature space without voxel-wise registration, while local-contrast reweighting emphasizes focal deviations over diffuse bilateral mismatch. The resulting deviation features are integrated with intrinsic target-side appearance through residual cross-attention and aggregated across slices for breast-side classification. On ODELIA, PRISM-Net achieved Macro AUC, Micro AUC, and quadratic weighted kappa values of 84.11 ± 2.33, 90.64 ± 1.61, and 60.94 ± 5.64 on the in-distribution test set, and 68.51 ± 4.54, 80.74 ± 2.68, and 43.45 ± 7.10 on the held-out institution, respectively, yielding the highest point estimates among the evaluated methods across the primary metrics. PRISM-Net also demonstrated favorable performance on an independent institutional cohort and background-complexity subsets, while ablation experiments supported the contributions of adaptive reference matching and focal deviation modeling. These findings support patient-specific contralateral reference learning as a clinically grounded strategy for breast DCE-MRI classification under heterogeneous background conditions.
